questions.help: Ask-once contract (FIX 8): this is the ONLY question this interview ever asks about plans/limits. It is asked only when the automatic probe could not determine a provider's concurrency (capacity.probe()['resource_profile']['pending_questions'] is non-empty); a fully detected client is never asked it. The machine lock lives in resource_profile.py -- the resource profile is THE store for this answer, and after it is recorded there the provider entry is marked locked and NO later run or probe refresh ever re-asks. A decline ('use conservative default') is recorded the same way and keeps the conservative default (3). Never paste credentials, API keys, endpoints, or any account identifier anywhere in this answer -- plan tier name only. MODEL CHOICE (operator requirement 2026-09-04): the client is never forced onto a department default. The workhorse/reasoning/qc/thinking subfields of this SAME turn record a client model plan through resource_profile.record_model_plan() into profile['model_plan']; model_router.resolve_route consults it AHEAD of CAPABILITY_CANDIDATES, which becomes the default for a client who declares nothing. A declared provider the profile does not carry, or a model that provider's wired inventory does not list, is REFUSED right here at intake (the answer returns an error naming the wired inventory it was checked against) -- never at dispatch time. Answering this turn again with different models UPDATES the plan and appends to the audit log; a client changing their workhorse never needs an operator. ROUTE HONESTY (FIX 18): when the client's route involves Ollama, this turn ALSO presents the numeric honesty block, rendered live by presentation_job.route_honesty from capacity.py's own tables -- never from numbers typed into this bank. It is shown ONCE per account-level answer set and carries, in plain terms: the concurrency their Ollama tier actually buys (CAP_TABLE today: $20/month -> 3 at a time; $100/month -> 8 at a time of the account's 10, with 2 kept in reserve), what that means in rounds of work for a deck of their size, the standing warning that Ollama routes, local or cloud, are materially slower for this workload than direct API routes (no multiplier is quoted, ever), and the standing recommendation: for best results, use OpenRouter or DeepSeek Direct, because neither route holds a deck back with a provider concurrency cap and on those routes the machine is the only limit. The engine has no measured per-slide time for the client's setup, so no minutes estimate is quoted -- say so plainly rather than inventing one. The client's decision is recorded in the resource profile either way (accepted or declined); declining is just keeping their Ollama selection in this same answer, it changes nothing about how the deck is handled, and the block is not shown again unless the client changes their selection.
questions.resolverHint: Feeds resource_profile.record_plan_answer(provider, plan) -- scripts/presentation_job/resource_profile.py IS the store for the plan tier, holding the tier, the cap-table ceiling and the ask-once lock in one per-provider entry (never in-repo, never printed verbatim -- redaction contract). The production writer is deck-intake-driver.py's _record_plan_tier() on THIS turn: it matches the tier against capacity.PLANS_BY_PROVIDER for each provider the probe still reports as owed an answer, records it per provider, and REFUSES the turn (naming the accepted tiers) rather than accepting a tier it cannot record. ASK ONLY when capacity.probe()['resource_profile']['pending_intake_ids'] contains 'resource_plan'; after record_plan_answer (or record_conservative_default for the decline) it is locked and pending_questions() returns empty forever, which is the ask-once proof surface. Probe refresh (apply_probe_refresh) updates detected fields WITHOUT touching the lock. The model subfields feed resource_profile.record_model_plan(plan, source='interview') -> profile['model_plan'] + profile['interview']['model_plan'] audit rows. They are deliberately NOT in storeTarget: the model plan lives in the secrets-adjacent profile store, never in the run directory's intake.json.

questions.prompt: What kind of presentation do you need?
questions.help: This single answer decides everything downstream -- deck type, creation mode, presentation mode, and audience mode are all derived automatically from it (see legacy_field_mapping at the top of this file). You never have to answer those separately. There is no default: this question must be answered by the client -- an unanswered or unrecognized answer must never be treated as 'from_scratch' or any other type.

value_labels.from_scratch: From scratch -- brainstorm and build new
value_labels.content_personal: From your content -- personal (one specific recipient)

questions.resolverHint: No default: if the owner says 'no preference' or does not answer, do NOT guess -- re-ask, or escalate to the operator. Landmine closed (2026-08-18): this question used to carry a JSON `default: from_scratch` that a required:false flip (or any consumer treating absence as approval) could silently re-arm, producing a webinar for every client who never actually answered. An absent or unrecognized presentation_type answer must fail closed -- see UngroundedDeckTypeError in intake_writer.py and _normalize_enum_value in deck-intake-driver.py, both of which now refuse to fabricate a value here. The driver derives deck_type, creation_mode, presentation_mode, and audience_mode from this ONE answer via derive_legacy_fields() (deck-intake-driver.py) the moment it is validated -- never ask those four as separate questions. 'content_personal' additionally requires recipient_name (asked immediately after, order 0.3) and extracted_substance before build (per _chk_mode); 'content_general' requires extracted_substance. 'signature': the driver asks ONE conditional follow-up ('signature_source', order 0.5: is this built from existing content?), sets deck_type:signature_presentation in working/copy/intake.json, and routes to the Signature Presentation Architect / brainstorming-buddy-presentations SIGNATURE mode, which is choice-first (QUICK vs IN-DEPTH) and then asks the SACRED 8 Questions + the frame-selection question ONE at a time -- never a batch (dumping them is AF-INTAKE-BATCH) -- assembling the answers into ONE atomic record per 51-signature-presentation/intake/sp-8-questions.json (deck-intake-driver.py signature mode). The frame is captured THERE as signature_frame (rulebook|vault|quest|original), not here. Director Mode A/B is NEVER asked -- it stays derived from whether source assets exist (director-of-presentations.md SOP 9.3). This question runs BEFORE the standard one-question-per-turn capture below; every question below behaves exactly as today regardless of presentation_type.

questions.prompt: What is the one core idea your existing material must convey?
questions.help: Asked only for the two CONTENT modes (content_personal / content_general). This is the SUBSTANCE the deck is extracted FROM -- build_deck.py's AF-MODE-UNSET gate refuses a content-mode deck that has none (SOP-MODE-00, P22-P29). It is the client's own words, never the assistant's summary.
questions.resolverHint: Ask ONLY when presentation_type is content_personal or content_general; auto-skipped for from_scratch and signature. The validated answer is lifted verbatim into working/copy/intake.json.extracted_substance by _apply_type_picker_derivation -- never paraphrased, never defaulted. There is no default: an empty answer must be re-asked.

value_labels.from_scratch: Building it from scratch with you
value_labels.existing_content: Converting existing content I already have

questions.resolverHint: Ask only when presentation_type=='signature'. Default if unanswered: from_scratch. On 'existing_content': the driver asks the SAME content_personal-vs-content_general follow-up implicitly via the normal signature 8-Questions flow; until that is known, creation_mode is set to content_general (the safer default -- never left unset per AF-MODE-UNSET) and corrected once the signature intake clarifies the audience. On 'from_scratch': creation_mode stays from_scratch (the signature default).

questions.prompt: Would you like the sales-and-checkout package alongside the presentation?
questions.help: Default YES. The sales page + checkout page + checkout order form is a standard upsell deliverable and one of the engine's fail-closed gates. The form ships as lead-capture (order form + follow-up workflow); live card charges need a connected merchant, otherwise the checkout phase reports an explicit actionable blocker while deck work continues. A 'no' is recorded as a CLIENT WAIVER with the client's own words -- it is never inferred from silence and never written by the assistant. A 'no' gates OUT the sales+checkout branch entirely.

value_labels.yes: Yes, build the sales page and checkout page

questions.resolverHint: Default 'yes' when the owner says 'whatever you recommend' or does not answer. Only an explicit 'no' opens the follow-up. Never mark 'no' on the client's behalf; never summarise their reason -- the follow-up answer is stored VERBATIM as the waiver's client_request_quote. A 'no' gates OUT the sales+checkout branch (deck-only or VSL-only run); a 'yes' enables the P-U-SALES-* / P-U-CHECKOUT-* / P-U-FORM-CHECKOUT phases.

questions.prompt: Would you like a video sales letter page?
questions.help: Default NO -- a VSL page requires the video to exist (see the VSL video dependency: the VSL page references the hosted webinar/video, so a video must be produced before the page build). Default stays 'no' unless the owner explicitly opts in. A 'yes' is a fail-closed gate; a 'no' is recorded as a CLIENT WAIVER with the client's own words -- it is never inferred from silence and never written by the assistant. A 'no' gates OUT the VSL branch entirely.
questions.resolverHint: Default 'no' (video must exist for a VSL page). Only an explicit 'yes' opens the VSL branch; a 'no' opens the follow-up. Never mark 'no' on the client's behalf; never summarise their reason -- the follow-up answer is stored VERBATIM as the waiver's client_request_quote. A 'yes' enables the P-U-VSL-* phases which wait on the video (V1) before the page build.

A 'no' gates OUT the email branch entirely: nothing is prepared at delivery.

questions.resolverHint: Default 'no'. Only an explicit 'yes' elects the Skill 50 delivery option; a 'no' opens the follow-up. Never mark 'no' on the client's behalf; never summarise their reason -- the follow-up answer is stored VERBATIM as the waiver's client_request_quote. waiver_field_mapping._comment: U026 — the CONSENT record. Each entry maps a gate key (see the engine's Gates class) to the intake question that captures the client's own decision, plus the conditional follow-up that captures their VERBATIM words when they decline. A gate may be waived ONLY by a record carrying a non-empty client_request_quote. Silence is NOT consent: every toggle here is required+block_gate, so --complete cannot pass while one is unanswered. prompt_floor and qc are deliberately ABSENT — a client cannot consent to a thinner prompt or a lower quality bar; those are craft floors, not options.
